source_text: Πρῶτος μὲν οὖν οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Χριστὸν ἀγαπῶν. δεύτερος δὲ ὁ τοὺς ἐκείνῳ πεπιστευκότας τιμῶν καὶ περιέπων. ὃ γὰρ ἄν τις εἰς μαθητὴν ἐργάσηται, τοῦτο εἰς ἑαυτὸν ὁ κύριος ἐκδέχεται καὶ πᾶν ἑαυτοῦ ποιεῖται. »δεῦτε, οἱ εὐλογημένοι τοῦ πατρός μου, κληρονομήσατε τὴν ἡτοιμασμένην ὑμῖν βασιλείαν ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου. ἐπείνασα γὰρ καὶ ἐδώκατέ μοι φαγεῖν, καὶ ἐδίψησα καὶ ἐδώκατέ μοι πιεῖν. καὶ ξένος ἤμην καὶ συνηγάγετέ με. γυμνὸς ἤμην καὶ ἐνεδύσατέ με, ἠσθένησα καὶ ἐπεσκέψασθέ με, ἐν φυλακῇ ἤμην καὶ ἤλθετε πρός με. τότε ἀποκριθήσονται αὐτῷ οἱ δίκαιοι λέγοντες· κύριε, πότε σε εἴδομεν πεινῶντα καὶ ἐθρέψαμεν, ἢ διψῶντα καὶ ἐποτίσαμεν; πότε δὲ εἴδομέν σε ξένον καὶ συνηγάγομεν. ἢ γυμνὸν καὶ περιεβάλομεν; ἢ πότε σε εἴδομεν ἀσθενοῦντα καὶ ἐπεσκεψάμεθα; ἢ ἐν φυλακῇ καὶ ἤλθομεν πρὸς σέ; ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ βασιλεὺς ἐρεῖ αὐτοῖς· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν. ἐφ᾿ ὅσον ἐποιήσατε ἑνὶ τούτων τῶν ἀδελφῶν μου τῶν ἐλαχίστων. ἐμοὶ ἐποιήσατε.« πάλιν ἐκ τῶν ἐναντίων τοὺς ταῦτα μὴ παρασχόντας αὐτοῖς εἰς τὸ πῦρ ἐμβάλλει τὸ αἰώνιον, ὡς αὐτῷ μὴ παρεσχηκότας.
thought_title: Christ receives service to his disciples as service to himself
orientation: Clement is explaining that the second way of loving Christ is to honor and care for those who have believed in him, and he quotes the judgment scene from Matthew 25 to show that Christ counts service to his least brothers as service to himself.
pass_a_gloss: First then this one is the [one] loving Christ. Second [is] the [one] honoring and caring for those who have believed in him. For whatever anyone may do to a disciple, this the Lord receives to himself and makes all [of it] his own. "Come, you blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from [the] foundation of [the] world. For I hungered and you gave me to eat, and I thirsted and you gave me to drink. And I was a stranger and you gathered me in. I was naked and you clothed me, I was sick and you visited me, I was in prison and you came to me. Then the righteous will answer him saying: Lord, when did we see you hungering and we fed [you], or thirsting and we gave [you] drink? When did we see you a stranger and we gathered [you] in? Or naked and we clothed [you]? Or when did we see you being sick and we visited [you]? Or in prison and we came to you? Answering, the king will say to them: Amen I say to you. Inasmuch as you did [it] to one of these my brothers the least, you did [it] to me." Again from the opposite [side] those not providing these things to them he throws into the fire the eternal, as [those] not having provided [them] to him.

choices.why: The verb means to treat with attentive care or tend to someone; 'caring for' captures the active solicitude Clement describes toward believers.
The verb means to accept or take to oneself; 'receives' keeps the sense that the Lord takes the deed as directed to himself.
The verb means to bring together or receive as a guest; 'gathered me in' preserves the hospitality sense of taking a stranger into one's home.
The phrase means 'to the extent that' or 'insofar as'; 'inasmuch as' is the standard English rendering for this judicial formula.
The phrase means 'from the contrary things' or 'on the other hand'; 'from the opposite side' keeps the contrast with the blessed who are welcomed.

pass_b_english: So the first person is the one who loves Christ. The second is the one who honors and cares for those who have believed in him. For whatever someone does for a disciple, the Lord receives as done to himself and makes it entirely his own. "Come, you who are blessed by my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. For I was hungry and you gave me food to eat; I was thirsty and you gave me something to drink; I was a stranger and you gathered me in; I was naked and you clothed me; I was sick and you visited me; I was in prison and you came to me." Then the righteous will answer him, saying, "Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you something to drink? When did we see you a stranger and gather you in, or naked and clothe you? When did we see you sick or in prison and come to you?" And the king will answer them, "Truly I tell you, inasmuch as you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me." Then, from the opposite side, he casts into the eternal fire those who did not provide these things to them, because they did not provide them to him.
